{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOLEgSIs8AAAABZeN2CA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm7fazhDFacM", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm7fa", "number": 35, "title": "Correct fixedFoveation bindings and restore legacy Three.js session startup", "body": "## Problem

At `dev` revision `30c35f3d0504b8af3d7a82ab57d79f15e899d158`, [layers.ts](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/30c35f3d0504b8af3d7a82ab57d79f15e899d158/src/polyfill/api/layers.ts) exposes `XRWebGLLayer.fixedFoveation` through a getter without a setter. PR #34 replaced a writable field with this getter. Strict-mode assignment consequently throws instead of accepting a supported no-op write. `XRProjectionLayer.fixedFoveation` remains a TypeScript readonly field that is writable in JavaScript, so assignment changes its reported value despite foveation being unsupported.

[Three.js r186 WebXRManager](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/9b4a2ac29c63ccb43fd51c5661f2f873ac2c39b8/src/renderers/webxr/WebXRManager.js) calls `setFoveation()` during session setup and assigns both layer variants. The legacy failure is a source-level deduction, not an observed application failure. Existing custom Three.js fixtures select projection layers even without requesting `layers`; they do not exercise the legacy fallback.

## Expected outcome

Both attributes reproduce their nullable-float binding contracts while honestly reporting unsupported foveation: reads return null and successfully converted writes have no effect. Legacy Three.js session setup and rendering succeed.

Apply this to Quest 3 `immersive-vr`, Quest MR and Android `immersive-ar`. Cover inline `XRWebGLLayer` on both profiles. Base layers support WebGL1/2; current projection rendering requires immersive WebGL2. Foveation has no separate feature descriptor. Preserve existing single-projection negotiation without `layers` and existing `layers` requirements for additional composition functionality.

## Context

Start from and target `dev`. Inspect `api/layers.ts`, the shared allocation-brand pattern in `api/interface-brand.ts`, constructor exposure in `CustomWebXRPolyfill.ts`, and `tests/webgl-layer.ts`/`tests/conformance.ts`. Keep changes focused on these attributes and necessary integration, generated bundle and inventory updates.

Use [Device CRD 2026-06-09 §11.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/CRD-webxr-20260609/#xrwebgllayer-interface), [Layers WD 2026-08-11 §3.5](https://www.w3.org/TR/2026/WD-webxrlayers-1-20260811/#xrprojectionlayer), and [WebIDL revision 622910c](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/blob/622910c67c724e362f71e8255a0380bade261acb/index.bs). Unsupported no-op behavior does not bypass WebIDL receiver validation or nullable-float conversion. [Pinned WPT Device IDL](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/e1859580b5fcf74940a18d2f783296b4961035e3/interfaces/webxr.idl) and [Layers IDL](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/e1859580b5fcf74940a18d2f783296b4961035e3/interfaces/webxrlayers.idl) corroborate both writable `float?` declarations; these sources are not execution evidence.

All 34 existing Issues/PRs are closed. [PR #34](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/pull/34) delivered owned framebuffers. Its [execution record](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/30c35f3d0504b8af3d7a82ab57d79f15e899d158/docs/webxr-framebuffer-validation-2026-10-24.json) reports 670 framebuffer assertions passing on Chromium 156.0.8078.4 and successful depth-enabled custom Three.js projection rendering. It explicitly excludes Firefox and official application execution. The depth-disabled projection client failure remains separate. Preserve these distinctions and the recorded framebuffer requirement corrections.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement enumerable, configurable prototype getter/setter pairs for both `fixedFoveation` attributes, without own data-field shadows. Genuine objects always read null; valid strict-mode assignments succeed without changing capability reporting, framebuffer/texture identity, dimensions or pixels.
- [ ] Validate the corresponding interface receiver before converting the value. Reject unrelated objects, prototype forgeries, proxies and the other layer interface with TypeError. Borrowed accessors accept genuine matching objects from another accessible injected same-origin realm; reuse the repository's allocation-brand approach where needed.
- [ ] Apply nullable `float` conversion before ignoring writes: null/undefined succeed; numeric strings, booleans and coercible objects convert; conversion runs once. NaN, infinities, finite values overflowing float32, Symbols and BigInts throw TypeError. Preserve exceptions thrown by coercion unchanged. Converted finite values below 0 or above 1 remain accepted no-ops with null readback.
- [ ] Keep this attribute independent of animation-callback activity and resource availability. Retained genuine objects preserve null/no-op behavior after session end, context loss and projection destruction; invalid conversions still fail. Access must not allocate, resurrect or modify GL resources.
- [ ] Add focused browser cases covering both attributes, conversion/brand precedence, cross-realm borrowing and retained-object lifetime. Cover all three immersive configurations, base-layer WebGL1/2, and inline base layers. Preserve existing resource, presentation and projection/quad assertions.
- [ ] Extend the existing Three.js fixture with an isolated legacy-capability configuration that actually selects `XRWebGLLayer` before renderer construction. Use unmodified Three.js library code, restore altered capability exposure in cleanup, and label the configuration as a harness adaptation. Across all three immersive profiles, demonstrate successful session setup, repeated `renderer.xr.setFoveation()` calls, null layer readback, rendered application pixels and clean shutdown. Retain projection-path coverage. Record the executed library version/source hashes and its relationship to the pinned r186 source; do not count this custom fixture as an official application scenario.
- [ ] The Coordinator performs implementation-stage `npm run build` and `npm run test:browser` containing these focused cases, inspects generated bundle changes, and records source/bundle provenance, browser/tool versions, actual outcomes, failures and skips. Update the capability inventory. Existing test code or historical passes cannot substitute for execution of the new cases. Tests and PR review remain Coordinator-owned.
- [ ] Record the original implementation assumption—null-only getters or TypeScript readonly fields suffice for unsupported reporting—and its correction: writable, branded, converted accessors are required before unsupported no-op handling. Retain the primary references and rationale in the Issue/PR. Correct any further mistaken AI-authored requirement with its original assumption, correction, primary evidence and rationale, without human approval or independent AI re-review. Preserve meaningful acceptance and the agreed goal.

## Optional validation

Exercise a pinned official Three.js example under the explicitly adapted legacy-capability configuration, recording exact sources and observed pixels. Firefox runtime coverage remains separate actionable work. No additional generic test rerun or independent AI re-review is requested.

## Required post-merge verification

None required.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WebXR API compatibility goal for
Quest 3 VR/MR and Android AR. Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance
criteria when primary specifications or measured evidence establish the correction.
Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.
